newsitem.title: USA: U.S. committee sets L.A. hearing on power outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. committee sets L.A. hearing on power outage.

text.p: A U.S. congressional subcommittee will hold a hearing Thursday in Los Angeles on the August 10 western states power outage, the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power announced Tuesday.
The Water and Power Subcommittee of the U.S. House of Representatives will conduct the first congressional hearing on the outage, which left four million people in nine states without power.

The subcommittee is holding the hearing because events at the Oregon-based Bonneville Power Administration - a federal agency - may have initiated the widespread blackout, the L.A. utility said in a statement.
The hearing aims to gather information about the August outage, events leading up to it, and the federal government's role and responsibility in preventing future outages.

Among those set to testify are Randall Hardy, head of the Bonneville Power Administration, Mark Bonsall, chairman of the Western Systems Coordinating Council, and John Velehradsky, director of engineering and technical services for the North Pacific Division of the Army Corp of Engineers.
